problem.after:
The review tool lists changed files by diffing against `HEAD`, and never checks that the repository has a commit. In a repository with no commit, `review snapshot` exits 1 with git's "bad revision 'HEAD'", which does not tell the user to commit first, so `/converge` cannot start fixing defects.

`/converge` finds defects in a project and then fixes them. Before each round of fixes, it runs `.ok-planner/bin/review snapshot`, which saves every file changed since `HEAD`, so a verifier can read only each fix's change. A new project that has run true-up, the suite's setup pass, but has made no commit has no `HEAD`. `review changed` with no `--base` takes `HEAD` the same way.

A driver, an agent that uses the product as a user would, made a scratch project with `git init` and true-up, filed two stories, and ran the drive-mode steps of `/converge` in order. `review snapshot --out <folder>/fix-1.json` printed `review: git diff --relative --name-status --no-renames HEAD -- . failed: fatal: bad revision 'HEAD'` and exited 1. After one commit, the same call printed `snapshot: 0 file(s)`, and every later step ran.

When one entry in the project's folder list is malformed, the review tool prints a note, reads the project root alone, and exits 0 instead of refusing. Every `/converge` run then hunts, checks, and certifies without the code in the other declared folders, and its report still shows the checks passing.

A project lists the folders it owns under the `folders` key of `.ok-planner/config.json`. One design decision, [decision:project-declares-its-folders](.ok-planner/design/decisions/project-declares-its-folders.md), says every tool that lists or scopes the project's code reads that list. Another, [decision:settings-have-no-code-defaults](.ok-planner/design/decisions/settings-have-no-code-defaults.md), says code that cannot use a setting refuses rather than fall back. The lint is the project's code checker. The review tool is the script `/converge` uses to list the files it hunts, checks, and certifies.

The review tool asks the lint to check the list. On a bad entry, it returns no folders and a note, and goes on. It does the same when node is not on PATH to run the lint. The tests tool reads its folders through the same function. `/converge`'s skill text tells the run to quote the note and go on, so nothing stops the run.

An agent declared `[".", "../shared", "../nope"]` and changed `shared/util.py`. The code still falls back the same way.

problem.after:
A documentation sprint records the commit it starts from but never compares it with the commit it was planned against, so a product change committed in between goes undocumented. The run's closing step, `docs stamp`, then marks that documentation current, so every later `/plan-docs` skips the change.

A docspec declares one kind of documentation the project keeps. Its stamp is the commit at which its documentation last passed a documentation sprint, as [decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window](.ok-planner/design/decisions/docspec-stamp-opens-the-window.md) says, and `/plan-docs`, the planning session, reads only what changed since the stamp. It writes a documentation sprint that opens with `Planned against commit <sha>`. Execution step 3 records the starting commit with `git rev-parse HEAD` and checks only for uncommitted paths. After the owner commits the run, `docs stamp --commit <sha>` writes that later commit as each planned docspec's stamp.

A driver, an agent that uses the product as a user would, planned a documentation sprint, committed a new `--loud` flag before running it, ran it, and stamped it. `docs window` then printed `docspec:guide ... status: current` and `docspec:faq ... status: current`, while `grep -c loud docs/guide.md docs/faq.md` printed 0.

problem.after:
`/ok-setup` shows the owner each choice its budget agent made alone, reruns the agent on each choice the owner overturns, and only then writes the test budget. Each `/converge` close instead files one issue per overturned choice for the next `/plan-sprint`. The owner decides whether `/ok-setup` keeps its own way.

`/ok-setup` sets up a project's testing. In one step an agent writes the test budget: the workers, the stack command, and the limits test runs keep. Its weak case, a narrow rerun that clears a whole round's leftover failure, does no lasting harm: every round counts leftovers, so a rerun that leaks again records the failure again, and certification still ends only on a passing whole-suite round ([decision:test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests](.ok-planner/design/decisions/test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests.md)), which drops every earlier failure and records its own. The flip case: if certifications show a leftover or stop failure that a narrow rerun cleared and the final whole-suite round found again, run after run, the loop is churning, and only the next whole-suite round should clear it.

options.text: Where the project holds no seed that testing.setup builds, no test-stage prompt or rule suggests a seed: the test writer, the speed reviewer, and the waste rule never name one, the test builds or reads its own data (such as a fixture), and no task closes blocked over a seed.

options.label: B
options.text: A support task that meets a seed request in a project with no seed creates the seed and the testing.setup step that builds it.

problem: Vetoed call i166 of sprint 2026-11-06-testing-in-the-sprint (stage i10-prompts, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-support.md, the seed bullet). As built, a project with no seed that testing.setup builds still gets seed entries suggested, and the suggestion stops the sprint. Four sites offer a seed with no check that one exists: the `seed` support change in skills/converge/prompts/test-write.md, the seed as 'the cheaper form' in skills/converge/prompts/test-speed.md, and {{TEST-WASTE-RULE}} in skills/_sprint/shared.md ('data the test only reads that the project's seed could hold'). When a test task asks for a seed entry, the write stage files a support task, and test-support.md tells it: 'Where the project holds no seed that testing.setup builds, add no entry: close blocked, naming the item and saying the project has no seed.' The write stage then refuses to refile a test task that waits on a task closed other than done, and the sprint template calls that refusal a genuine blocker under step 11, so execution stops and waits on the owner. That breaks the rule that no step of a sprint waits on a person. The owner's choice: what the test stages do about a seed where the project has none.

ruling.text: is there is no seed available, then it should be a no-op, not even suggested. not blocked.

title: Whether test stages suggest a seed entry in a project that has no seed
